support.label: Exact, literal wording
support.demo:
verifyToken reads JWT_SECRET.
It is unset when the tests run.

support.label: Explain terms as you use them
support.demo: The token is a JWT — a signed string the server can check without a database lookup.

support.label: Show a worked example
support.demo:
Here it is done once, in full:
  jwt.verify(token, secret)  ->  { userId: 'u_12' }

support.label: Analogies, then the literal version
support.demo:
Analogy: the cache is a fixed-size queue.
Literal: maxSize is 500; entry 501 evicts entry 1.

support.label: Spell out the reasoning
support.demo: Set JWT_SECRET in test/setup.ts, because verifyToken reads it and an unset secret is what returns 401.

support.label: One name per thing
support.demo: verifyToken, every time. Not “the handler”, not “the auth thing”, not “it”.

support.label: Say what it does before the command
support.demo:
This adds one line to test/setup.ts:
  process.env.JWT_SECRET = 'test-secret'

support.label: Summary first, detail underneath
support.demo:
The 401 comes from auth.ts:47.
Cause and fix below.

support.label: Short labelled sections
support.demo:
Cause
  JWT_SECRET is unset in the tests.

Fix
  One line, below.

support.demo:

Say “why” for the reasoning, “more” for the other two files.
support.defers_note: Holds detail back until you ask for it.

support.label: Keep the diagram, symbols and meanings connected
support.demo:
s_next = f(s_now, event)
Symbol | Meaning | Example
s_now | the stored state | count = 2
event | the input asking for a change | increment
f | the rule for the next state | add one
s_next | the state after the rule | count = 3

support.demo: In code terms: the state machine is a reducer, state_next = reduce(state_now, event). Where it stops: a reducer must be pure; this one may read a clock.
